clue.text: Repeatedly set fire to beams, manually controlled

parts.note: to torch something is to set fire to it
the phrase used again: to light something is also to set fire to it

explanation.surface: An arsonist keeps setting fire to the timbers of a building, doing it all by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' tells you to use 'set fire to' twice, with two different synonyms; 'beams' are not timbers but rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The rays thrown by a handheld lamp are steered by the holder's hand.

clue.text: Casual worker takes remaining book on to island

parts.note: an odd item is one left over, remaining from a set
Job is a book of the Old Testament
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A temporary employee picks up a spare volume before heading to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hired for occasional small tasks is a temporary, casual labourer.

clue.text: Noise made by chain in prison

definitions.meaning: the short metallic ringing sound of links knocking together

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the sound of metal on metal and old slang for a jail.

clue.text: Refuse to go in here

parts.note: read as a stubborn refusal to enter, but 'Refuse' is the noun meaning rubbish, and this is where rubbish should be put

explanation.definitionFit: A street receptacle is the proper place for rubbish to be dropped.

clue.text: Old Testament character under gallery in religious show

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed under another comes after it

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
Lot, Abraham's nephew, whose wife was turned to a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: A biblical figure is pictured beneath a gallery in a church pageant.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GODS is the cheapest, highest seating in a British theatre. A GOD SLOT is a period of broadcast time set aside for religious programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular broadcast slot given over to religious programming.

clue.text: Sweet wine or tea pronounced passable

indicators.note: the word tea is to be taken as it sounds, which is the name of a letter

parts.note: said aloud, tea sounds like the letter T
okay means acceptable, passable

explanation.surface: Someone samples a dessert wine, or else a cup of tea, and declares it acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich sweet Hungarian dessert wine from the Tokaj region.

clue.text: As company doctor, examine thoroughly

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Acting as the firm's medical officer, someone gives a thorough check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through something minutely, as with a fine-toothed instrument, is a meticulous search.

clue.text: How to kick drug dependence? Don't be daft!

definitions.meaning: taken literally: stop taking the substance you are hooked on
an exclamation telling someone to stop talking nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means stop using something and is also a scornful retort to nonsense.

clue.text: People as stuck-up as they are intelligent?

definitions.text: People as stuck-up as they are intelligent?

parts.note: men means people in general

indicators.note: in a down clue, something stuck up is turned upwards, so the word as reads from the bottom

explanation.surface: A dig at clever people for being as snobbish as they are bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck-up' looks like snobbery but reverses AS to SA in a down clue; the whole clue is also a teasing description of the high-IQ society.
explanation.definitionFit: The society admits only people scoring highly on intelligence tests, whom the clue teases as snobbish.

clue.text: Allowed to be taken in

definitions.meaning: let in as a member, entrant or patient

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both conceded or permitted and let in at the door.

clue.text: Exotic garment of little girl in family circle

indicators.note: the girl's name sits inside the word for family

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
Mo is a short form of the girl's name Maureen
O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A young daughter is surrounded by her relatives in a family gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose wide-sleeved Japanese robe, foreign to Western eyes.

clue.text: His betters support him — in literary work, that is

parts.note: a book is a written work
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A writer is propped up by superiors who appear in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'betters' looks like superiors but means people who bet, and a bookmaker depends on their stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker lives off the stakes placed by gamblers.

clue.text: New way salesman dramatically takes in inexpert female

indicators.note: the salesman's surname holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: Willy Loman is the salesman in Arthur Miller's play Death of a Salesman

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters of way

explanation.surface: A theatrical salesman with novel methods wins over a woman who knows little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dramatically' says the salesman comes from the stage, Arthur Miller's Willy; 'New' gives AYW and 'takes in' puts it inside his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who is not a professional or specialist, or not a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Prophet's body returned

indicators.note: the word for body comes back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: soma is the body, as distinct from the mind

explanation.surface: A holy man's corpse is brought home.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor Old Testament prophet with a book named after him.

clue.text: Author setting a book inside ancient Asian city

indicators.note: the article and the gospel go within the writer's name

parts.note: George Sand, the French novelist
Mark is a gospel, a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A novelist chooses to set a story in a historic city of Central Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on the Silk Road in Uzbekistan, among the oldest inhabited in Central Asia.

clue.text: To provide an early meal, .courage paid off

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
to fee someone is to pay them, so paid off can be read as fee'd

explanation.surface: Showing nerve in serving breakfast was rewarded.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE is British slang for courage. An infant's earliest meals may come from a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a baby milk from a bottle is to supply its first meals in life.

clue.text: Port in extremely short supply, frequently

parts.note: when supply is at its very shortest it is lowest
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A harbour town is in desperately short supply, and often.
explanation.walkthrough: LOWESTOFT is a port in Suffolk, the most easterly town in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing port on the Suffolk coast of eastern England.

clue.text: How one of sixteen may be taken on board

definitions.text: How one of sixteen may be taken on board

parts.words: How one of sixteen may be taken on board
parts.note: the board is a chessboard and the sixteen are the pawns; one may be captured by a special move after it advances two squares

explanation.definitionFit: The chess rule lets a pawn capture an enemy pawn that has just passed it by moving two squares.

clue.text: Theatrical performance without dialogue

parts.note: a show with no conversation because there is only a single performer to speak

explanation.definitionFit: A solo show has a single performer, so nobody to hold a conversation with.

clue.text: New Amsterdam today, in part, has swallowed a Dutch town

indicators.note: the district takes the letter a down inside itself

parts.note: New Amsterdam is now New York, and Harlem is a district of it

explanation.surface: A New York neighbourhood has absorbed a town from the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: New York was once New Amsterdam, and its Harlem was named after the Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in North Holland near Amsterdam, after which the New York district is named.

clue.text: South Americans in one express heading West

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: to put something is to express it in words
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller on a fast train goes westward towards South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like a fast train but is the verb to put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: A people of Brazil and Paraguay along the Amazon and coast.

clue.text: Inspiring quality is found in Daily Mail? Not half!

parts.note: a daily or char is a cleaning lady
taken as written

indicators.note: only the first half of the word mail is kept

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader wonders whether magnetism is found in the Daily Mail, and gets the reply: not half!
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' in Britain is a cleaner, as is a CHAR; 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so' but here halves MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism that inspires devotion in others.

clue.text: Breaking in-is the American style of robbery

indicators.note: breaking the words up lets their letters be reassembled

explanation.surface: Burglary by forced entry is how robbers do it in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for a robbery is chiefly American in origin.

clue.text: A lot of swimmers in shallow water

definitions.meaning: a sandbank or place where the sea is not deep

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a large school of fish and a sandbank making the sea shallow.

clue.text: Second church exists, ultimately from this

definitions.text: Second church exists, ultimately from this

parts.note: is means exists

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter of the word from

explanation.surface: A second church comes into being as the result of a split.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a breakaway church is born out of a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A split in a church is what produces a rival second congregation.

clue.text: Short hair this country sent up in verse form!

indicators.note: the word hair is cut short, losing its final letter
in a down clue, sent up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, is this country for a British setter

explanation.surface: A crew cut in this country is mocked in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' looks like mockery but reverses UK to KU.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese poem of three lines of five, seven and five syllables.

clue.text: Star group includes a strident female

indicators.note: the constellation takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: Virgo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A celebrity band has a shrill woman among its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star group' looks like a band of celebrities but is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: A domineering, bad-tempered woman, a shrew.

clue.text: Coward? Just the reverse — I died a Spartan leader

definitions.text: Coward? Just the reverse — I died a Spartan leader

indicators.note: the playwright's first name is to be read backwards

parts.note: Noel Coward, the English playwright

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Greek king protests that far from being a coward, he died as leader of Sparta.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spartan king held the pass at Thermopylae to the death, the very reverse of cowardice.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Sparta who fell defending the pass at Thermopylae in 480 BC.

clue.text: Boss in establishment expected to have good breeding

definitions.meaning: a raised ornamental knob or nail head

definitions.text: establishment expected to have good breeding
definitions.meaning: a farm where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a raised knob and a horse-breeding farm.

clue.text: A term of French — that seems most appropriate

definitions.text: A term of French — that seems most appropriate

parts.words: A term of French — that seems most appropriate
parts.note: a French expression meaning exactly the right word for the occasion

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names the precisely fitting word for a context.
